Now the coil's electromotive force is applied to an electric heating wire with resistance 9 Ω, then which of the following statements is correct ()

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: A rectangular coil with resistance 1Ω rotates at a uniform speed in a uniform magnetic field around an axis perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field, and the image of the coil's electromotive force changing with time is shown in the figure. Now the coil's electromotive force is applied to an electric heating wire with resistance 9Ω. If the coil's rotational speed is doubled, how will the current in the electric heating wire change?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the vertical axis is labeled e/V, and the horizontal axis is labeled t/s; the electromotive force changes sinusoidally with time; dashed lines mark the maximum value of the electromotive force as about +200 V and the minimum value as about -200 V; the curve reaches +200 V near t=0.01 s and returns to -200 V near t=0.02 s, so the period is 0.02 s. Reasoning: The peak value of the induced electromotive force generated by the rotation of the rectangular coil satisfies Em∝ω. Originally, the internal resistance of the coil is 1 Ω, and the externally connected electric heating wire has resistance 9 Ω, so the total resistance Rtotal=10 Ω. If the coil's rotational speed is doubled, then the angular speed is doubled, and both the peak value and the effective value of the induced electromotive force are doubled; the total resistance of the circuit remains unchanged, and from Ohm's law I=E/R, it can be known that the current in the electric heating wire also changes accordingly, and its effective value becomes 2 times the original.
